# Pack: OpenTofu and Spacelift

Status: written 2026-10-30 (issue #82, under #78) from the maintainer's measured lessons and vendor documentation, never from model memory. The pack benchmark of #73 is pending, so treat this as a checklist. Every claim is VERIFIED (a vendor page read on the date shown, or a run the notes record) or INFERRED (reason given).

## Limits

1. **Plan before apply.** No apply, destroy, `-auto-approve`, run confirm or stack delete without a plan the maintainer has read. Approval is the maintainer's own message or his own click in the Spacelift UI; a green check, another agent's verdict or a note in a file is not approval.
2. **Never apply to a live system without the maintainer.** You prepare the change, run `plan`, read it and hand it over. He applies, or says go in his own message for that exact plan. A rejected command is not permission to reach the same effect another way. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11: the host's auto-mode classifier blocked run creation and stack deletion; the maintainer did those steps in the UI.)
3. **Every plan names its blast radius and its rollback.** Blast radius: each resource to create, change, destroy or replace, what depends on it, what it costs. Rollback: the exact step that restores service, and a line for what it cannot restore (data, addresses, tokens). Spacelift cannot stop a confirmed run, so decide the rollback before the confirm. (Source: Spacelift tracked-run page, "Confirmed", read 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
4. **Read-only by default.** The Spacelift MCP session starts with `mcp:read` only (see the next section). Write (`mcp:write`) is granted per named task and dropped when the task ends.
5. **Plan the whole job's access once.** List every scope or token the job needs, ask for the union, and return to read-only afterwards. One DNS vendor's account-scoped token could not carry zone permissions and no token could be limited to one project, so learn a grant's shape before the job. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-25, observed.)

## Spacelift MCP: read-only versus write

The server lives at the `/mcp` path of the account host (`https://<account>.app.spacelift.io/mcp`). The old `/intent/mcp` path stays available only until 2026-08-01 and is gone after it. (Source: https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/intelligence/spacelift-mcp.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)

| Tool | What it does | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `discover` | browse the GraphQL schema | `mcp:read` |
| `query` | read-only GraphQL queries | `mcp:read` |
| `provider` | read provider, resource and data-source schemas | `mcp:read` |
| `mutate` | GraphQL mutations: stacks, policies, runs | `mcp:read` plus `mcp:write` |
| `intent` | create, update, delete, refresh, import, resume and read cloud resources | `mcp:read` plus `mcp:write` |

- A read-only session can introspect the API and read Spacelift and cloud state; it cannot change anything. Asking for `intent` turns `provider` on. A `tools` query parameter narrows the set further. (VERIFIED, same page.)
- Authentication is browser OAuth (interactive, short-lived token) or a `spacectl`-issued bearer token (headless). What the session may do also follows RBAC and login policies, so a scope is a ceiling, not a grant. (VERIFIED, same page.)
- **Rule:** open the session with `mcp:read`. A task that needs `mutate` or `intent` names the stack or resource, the change and the end condition before write is requested. Each mutation needs a fresh explicit yes. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10: every mutate needed a fresh yes.)

## Stacks: one explicit stanza each

- **Rule:** one `resource "spacelift_stack" "<name>"` block per stack, every setting spelled out (deletion protection, autodeploy, managed state, tool version, labels, `prevent_destroy`, role attachments), so a stanza can be copied, pasted and tweaked without touching a shared block. Do not drive stacks from one `for_each`.
- **Failure that taught it:** a single `for_each` stack resource applied shared settings (deletion protection, managed state, tool version, `prevent_destroy = true`) to every stack, so one stack's change meant editing the block all stacks share. The maintainer notes that `lifecycle.prevent_destroy` must be a literal and cannot come from a variable, so only per-stack blocks can set it per stack. (Source: maintainer note on the stack-factory redo, 2026-10-10; the literal rule is INFERRED against the vendor, whose page defines `prevent_destroy` but does not say it must be a literal.)
- **Safety rules live as assertions, not as structure.** Keep "autodeploy is false for managed stacks" and "only the factory stack holds space-admin" as `tofu test` assertions per stack, so a copy that drops a setting turns red. (Source: same note; OpenTofu `tofu test` runs `*.tftest.hcl` assertions, https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/test/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- `prevent_destroy` rejects a plan that destroys the object, but removing the whole resource block removes the protection too. (Source: https://opentofu.org/docs/language/resources/behavior/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)

## Plan and apply

- **Read the plan, not the summary.** Search it for replace and destroy before anything else. A refactor meant to be a no-op must plan as moves only; if any object is replaced, discard the run. Record a rename with a `moved` block so state follows it. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-16: after a module refactor the first tracked run had to show moves only; OpenTofu refactoring page, https://opentofu.org/docs/language/modules/develop/refactoring/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- **Apply the plan that was read.** `tofu plan -out=FILE`, inspect it with `tofu show FILE`, then `tofu apply FILE`; applying a saved plan takes its actions without prompting. A saved plan can hold sensitive values in cleartext, so treat the file as a secret. `-detailed-exitcode` returns 0 for no changes, 1 for error, 2 for changes. (Source: https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/plan/ and /apply/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- **`-auto-approve` and autodeploy are only as safe as the policies behind them.** Spacelift applies on its own only when autodeploy is on and no plan policy warns; keep autodeploy off for live stacks. (Source: https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/run/tracked.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- **Plan policies:** the vendor's guidance is to deny when the run is PROPOSED and warn when it is TRACKED, with a human deciding on warnings. A destroy guard (deny on protected resources) and an autodeploy guard were designed but not built when last recorded, so no measured result exists here (INFERRED). (Source: https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/policy/terraform-plan-policy.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED for the guidance.)
- **Check the run state before triggering anything.** A dependency that finishes starts a run on the dependent stack by itself, so a second trigger duplicates it, and the maintainer sometimes confirms in the UI before an agent does. Read the run state first. Unlock a locked stack before a change, and say so. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-11.)
- **A merge outside a stack's project root starts no run.** Use the stack's sync of the commit and then trigger the run, or declare project globs for shared paths such as `modules/**`. Globs only trigger; they do not mount files. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10, observed; https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/stack/stack-settings.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- **Destructive runs go to the maintainer.** Destroying resources (`stackDelete` with destruction, or a destroy task) is his step in the UI. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11.)
- **Look up what exists; do not recreate it.** A create failed with a 422 because the key already existed; the stack now looks it up by name. Check the provider's API for what exists and what the region offers (one region lacked the chosen size). (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11.)
- **Read the vendor's own Terraform guide first** when wiring an agent or connector: a piped installer in cloud-init left the service dead, the vendor's published pattern worked (the pipe as cause is INFERRED). (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10.)

## State and drift

- **State is sensitive.** It holds resource IDs and all attributes, including initial passwords. Never print or commit it. Prefer remote state; with local state the file is plain-text JSON. (Source: https://opentofu.org/docs/language/state/sensitive-data/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- **Edit state through `tofu state`, never by hand.** `tofu import` and `tofu state rm` change the one-to-one binding between configuration and remote objects, and you then own the matching delete or re-import. Say so in the plan. A default network the provider cannot delete was removed from state rather than destroyed. (Source: https://opentofu.org/docs/language/state/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED; maintainer notes, 2026-10-11.)
- **Drift** is the gap between the desired and the real state: an outside actor changed something, or an external data source moved. Spacelift detects it by running scheduled proposed runs, and can reconcile with a tracked run that obeys autodeploy and plan policies. Detection needs a paid tier and private workers; check before promising it. The policy input carries `drift_detection`, so a plan policy can warn and force a human to look before reconciling. (Source: https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/stack/drift-detection.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED. No drift schedule was run on the maintainer's free account; nothing about its behavior there is measured.)
- **Without drift detection:** `tofu plan -refresh-only` updates state to match changes made outside OpenTofu, for example during an incident; it changes state, not infrastructure, so read it first. `-refresh=false` ignores outside changes and can give an incomplete plan; never use it to make a plan look clean. (Source: https://opentofu.org/docs/cli/commands/plan/, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- Reconcile by changing the code or reverting the outside change, never by editing state to silence a report.

## Secrets and the pull-request boundary

- **Load secrets only on tracked runs from the default branch.** A hook script and its config come from the pull request branch, so on a proposed run from a fork they are attacker-controlled. The boundary must be a Spacelift push policy (`propose` or `ignore`, never trusting forks), not the script. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10; https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/policy/push-policy.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED for `propose` and `ignore`.)
- **A public pull request's proposed-run check can leak the account subdomain** in its URL; fix it with a push policy. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10, observed.)
- **Masking works one line at a time.** A multi-line value (a PEM key) is not masked. Chain hook commands with `&&`, not newlines or `;`. (Source: https://docs.spacelift.io/concepts/stack/stack-settings.html, fetched 2026-10-30, VERIFIED.)
- **Check what the plan provides before designing on it.** The free account had no OIDC token in runs (checked with a task), so a read-only service token in a context was used. Calendar token expiries. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-10; plan-dependent.)

## Done means observed

A provider call that returned success is not the end state. Attaching a custom domain through one vendor's API returned 200 while the domain stayed pending with no DNS record and the site answered an error; the record had to be created and the domain re-checked. Read the end state (the domain says active and the public URL serves), and report the evidence. (Source: maintainer notes, 2026-10-25, observed through the vendor API.)

## What this pack does not cover

- Provider design: DigitalOcean, AWS, Azure and GCP sizing, networking and costs. Those packs are planned under #78.
- Twingate access paths and Doppler secret handling (planned in #78); only the Spacelift side of secrets is here.
- Spacelift Intent in depth, blueprints, worker pools, billing and plan limits; Terragrunt, Pulumi, Ansible, CloudFormation, Kubernetes; state encryption, backend migration and OpenTofu upgrades.
- A security review or audit of a stack: use the `threat-model` pack and the reviewers. Never claim an audit.
- GitHub Actions workflow hygiene: use `gha-security-dast`.

## How to verify (commands)

- **Plan read:** `tofu plan -detailed-exitcode -out=plan.bin` and check its exit code (0 none, 2 changes, 1 error), then `tofu show plan.bin | grep -nE 'must be replaced|will be destroyed'`. The report quotes every hit.
- **No apply slipped in:** `grep -nE 'tofu (apply|destroy)|auto-approve|stackDelete|runConfirm' <report-or-script>` returns nothing unless the brief names the task and the maintainer's go.
- **One stanza per stack:** `grep -c 'resource "spacelift_stack"' stacks.tf` equals the number of stacks, and `grep -n 'for_each' stacks.tf` shows none on `spacelift_stack`.
- **Safety assertions bite:** run `tofu test`, flip one stack's `autodeploy` to true in a scratch copy, and the test must go red; restore and show a clean tree.
- **MCP scope:** the session's tool list shows only `discover`, `query` and `provider` before a named write task.
- **Privacy:** no account subdomain, token, state excerpt, IP address or stack name in the report; run the placeholder sweep.
